case_title: State of Maharashtra v. Ramlal Devappa Rathod
accused_victim_relationship: Land/village dispute rival; accused were villagers who formed the mob (no closer relationship described)
statutory_provisions: IPC ss.147, 148, 302, 307, 324, 326, 427, 435, 436, 452 read with s.149 (s.395 also listed in the charge-sheet per the judgment)
weapon: Swords, axes, sticks, stones and sattur
evidence_type: Eyewitness (sole eye-witness PW12), medical (post-mortem), recovery of weapons on disclosure, spot panchnama, damage to houses
confession: No confession stated. Disclosure statements of A-1, A-2, A-3, A-29 and A-30 led to recovery of blood-stained weapons; the Court relied on the recovery as one circumstance
aggravating_circumstances: Assault by a mob; victim chased from place to place and assaulted with multiple chop wounds and head injuries
trial_court_outcome: Convicted 8 accused under ss.147, 148, 302, 307, 326, 324, 427, 435, 436, 452 r/w 149 IPC; life imprisonment under s.302 r/w 149; other accused acquitted
high_court_outcome: Appeal (Criminal Appeal No. 885 of 2001) allowed; all 8 convicted accused acquitted
offence_finally_established: For A-1, A-2, A-3, A-12, A-29 and A-30: ss.147, 148, 302, 307, 326, 324, 427, 435, 436, 452 r/w s.149 IPC. For A-7 and A-10 acquittal stands (appeal dismissed)
neutral_facts: The victim was attacked at a village temple by a large group of villagers at about dawn, after prayers, and was struck with a sword. The accused, part of the crowd, chased him from place to place, including to the homes of relatives, where relatives and others were also assaulted. The attackers removed roof tiles and tin sheets to reach him, dragged him into a field and assaulted him with swords, axes and a sattur. Houses in the area were damaged and some set on fire, and documents, gold ornaments and cash were taken or burnt. Family members took the victim to hospital, where he was found dead. The post-mortem recorded multiple chop and incised wounds, skull fractures and sub-dural haematoma, with the cause of death given as hemorrhage and shock due to multiple chop wounds with head injury. The victim's brother lodged a complaint naming thirty-four persons and attributing overt acts to some. The spot panchnama recorded blood stains at the temple, the well, a road and the houses. After disclosure statements by several accused, blood-stained weapons were recovered the day after the incident. At trial, most eye-witnesses, including close relatives, were declared hostile on identity. The sole eye-witness, the victim's wife, described the incident in stages and identified specific accused. Her account was said to be supported by the medical evidence and other material.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from multiple chop wounds, skull fractures and brain injury; post-mortem recorded 13 external wounds and internal head injuries
number_of_offences: 11 charged (ss.147, 148, 302, 307, 324, 326, 395, 427, 435, 436, 452 r/w 149); 10 finally upheld for six accused (s.395 not among the convictions)
financial_property_loss: Victim's house documents burnt; gold ornaments and cash taken; damage to relatives' houses (amount not quantified)
motive: alleged: dispute over village agricultural land held by a society of which the victim's family were members
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony of sole eye-witness PW12 (victim's wife), including the nine stages of the incident and identification of six accused; medical evidence; spot panchnama; recovery of blood-stained weapons on disclosure statements (supported by investigating officer PW18); damage to houses
witness_credibility: PW12 found natural, consistent and reliable; her failure to be present earlier explained by a warrant, and lack of physical injuries not fatal to her account. Hostile witnesses' reluctance attributed to intensity of incident
post_offence_conduct: Disclosure statements leading to recovery of blood-stained weapons the day after the incident; Court treated it as a relevant circumstance
trial_duration: offence: 30.04.2000; trial judgment: 06.10.2001; High Court: 22.06.2006; Supreme Court: 29.09.2015
legal_representation: Appellant (State of Maharashtra): Shankar Chillarge, Sonia Shankar Chillarge, Aniruddha P. Mayee. Respondents: Meenakshi Arora, Mahima, Anjani Kumar Jha, Vinay Naware, Dr. R.R. Deshpande, Yuvraj Gaikwad
investigation_status: FIR registered; investigation, spot panchnama, post-mortem, recoveries and charge-sheet against thirty-four persons; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: 8 convicted (life under s.302 r/w 149). High Court: acquitted all 8. Supreme Court: appeal partly allowed; convictions of 6 (A-1, A-2, A-3, A-12, A-29, A-30) restored; acquittal of A-7 and A-10 confirmed
prosecution_argument: Sole eye-witness testimony (PW12) is reliable and corroborated; reliance on Masalti was not called for; High Court's assessment was erroneous
defence_argument: PW12's statement under s.161 CrPC was not recorded the same day; she had no injuries so her presence was doubtful; she was tutored at the police station; Masalti requires corroboration by at least one eye-witness in mob violence
legal_principle_applied: Conviction may rest on a sole witness if confidence-inspiring and corroborated; Masalti test applies only to vicarious liability without specific overt acts; s.149 membership suffices for vicarious liability; recoveries may be proved through the investigating officer
precedent_relied_upon: Relied: Mohd Aslam v. State of Maharashtra (2001) 9 SCC 362; Anter Singh v. State of Rajasthan (2004) 10 SCC 657; State of U.P. v. Kishan Pal (2008) 16 SCC 73; Amerika Rai v. State of Bihar (2011) 4 SCC 676. Referred: State of Haryana v. Inder Singh (2002) 9 SCC 537; Joseph v. State of Kerala (2003) 2 SCC 465; Ram Naresh v. State of Chhattisgarh (2012) 11 SCC 257. Masalti v. State of U.P. (1964) 8 SCR 133 held inapplicable; Dan Singh, Baddi Venkata Narasayya, Binay Kumar Singh distinguished; Mrinal Das and Inder Singh (2015) held inapplicable
other_sentence_order: Six convicted accused directed to be taken into custody forthwith; Criminal Misc. Petition No. 6303 of 2015 (based on Sessions Case No. 359 of 2003) rejected
